scope: Independent AI Golden SOP content review of eight unselected Author A drafts at the exact listed file hashes. No human, audio-listening, device, live, or publication sign-off.

structuralChecks.sourceProvenance: All eight exact source occurrence IDs, expressions and source sentences match source-inventory; target regex finds the intended form in each full source sentence.
structuralChecks.lessonContract: Fresh build and --check both pass: 8 lessons, 48 assessed questions, 32 audio requests, 0 structural review flags. Seven steps and six assessed questions are present per lesson.
structuralChecks.targetAndReply: Exactly one target-bearing golden reply appears among each lesson’s four options; pragmatic validity requires repair in 2519 and source grounding is weak in 2524.
structuralChecks.writingGlossary: All eight changed-context tasks have two complete bilingual model answers and five exact answer-derived non-target glossary spans; all spans were independently re-sliced from the actual model strings. The first 2527 English model has an ambiguous pronoun.
structuralChecks.audioText: Each lesson has four distinct requested texts (listening, speaking and two takeaways); every one contains a target regex match. This confirms the request list, not generated audio quality or approved voice.
structuralChecks.editorialRead: Read all six assessed question keys/options, four-valid reply sets, Chinese pairs, changed writing context/models, brief sense boundary and neighboring senses. The listed findings are specific repairs needed before selection.

findings.evidence: Across all eight records, brief.grammar is only a quoted example sentence (for example 2519: “The hurt may run deeper than a quick apology can address.”). The register fields describe metaphor or usage boundaries but do not consistently specify neutral/formal/informal setting or likely speaker/listener.
findings.problem: Golden SOP P81 requires the grammatical pattern, natural forms, register and likely speaker/listener to be recorded before authoring. The detector regex encodes some forms, but it does not replace a reviewer-readable pattern and use-context brief.
findings.repair: For each lesson, state subject/object frame, inflections and permissible pronouns/articles in brief.grammar; record register and natural speaker/listener situation in brief.register or an explicit schema field. Keep target regex and all assessed copy consistent; this is a brief-completeness repair, not a request to rewrite all exercises.

findings.evidence: Prompt asks “Why might Nora need to rebuild trust even after apologising?” Option d says “Respecting her friend’s privacy over time may help repair the relationship.”
findings.problem: Option d gives a repair method, not a reason Nora still needs to rebuild trust. It therefore fails the SOP four-pragmatically-valid-replies requirement even though its advice is sensible.
findings.repair: Replace d with a direct reason grounded in the friend’s continued reluctance to share private news; preserve one target-bearing golden option and update the Chinese as an exact pair.

findings.evidence: The listening model ends “The hurt may run deeper than the quick apology reached.” The source guide says “than a quick apology can address.”
findings.problem: “An apology reached” is strained English here and makes the first audio model less natural than the source-supported formulation. The Chinese already conveys what an apology can address.
findings.repair: Use natural comparative wording such as “The hurt may run deeper than a quick apology can address,” then reconfirm Chinese and regenerate the changed listening audio request.

findings.evidence: Model begins “The software compared rent and capacity, but it could not think on their behalf about older guests’ access …”; no people have been named as the antecedent of “their” in the English answer. Chinese explicitly says “替籌委會”, supplying an actor absent from English.
findings.problem: The answer is intended to stand alone in a changed-context writing model. The unclear pronoun weakens its naturalness, and the translation adds a specific referent that the English does not provide.
findings.repair: Name the committee/organisers in the English model before “their behalf” (or change to a clearly anchored “our behalf”), align the Chinese, and recompute any affected exact glossary spans and audio/target checks.

findings.evidence: English model: “The message can sting when it seems to erase someone’s effort.” Chinese: “簡短評論若似乎抹去別人的努力，也可能令人刺痛。”
findings.problem: The translation adds “簡短評論” (“brief comment”), which is not specified by “the message”, and changes the referent from a message to a comment.
findings.repair: Use “那句話” or “那則訊息” and preserve the conditional/uncertainty; the English model and target span can remain unchanged.

findings.evidence: Source says no cancellation alert reached waiting passengers. Option d states as fact “They had to find the changed sailing information elsewhere.”
findings.problem: The passengers’ search elsewhere is plausible but not established by the listening scene. A four-valid reply should be grounded in given evidence, particularly when it answers why confidence fell.
findings.repair: Replace d with a source-grounded cause, for example their inability to rely on promised schedule alerts; pair the Chinese with the revised English and keep golden c as the only target-bearing option.
